current_object.title: Complex plane-wave fields: real parts of complex exponentials
current_object.statement: Fix $\mathbf k\in\mathbb R^3$, $\omega>0$ and $\mathbf e,\mathbf b\in\mathbb C^3$. Writing $\exp$ for the complex exponential, $\operatorname{Re}$ for the real part and $\mathbf k\cdot\mathbf x$ for the Euclidean inner product, define for each $t\in\mathbb R$ the real vector fields $$\mathbf x\mapsto\operatorname{Re}\bigl[\mathbf e\exp(i(\mathbf k\cdot\mathbf x-\omega t))\bigr],\qquad \mathbf x\mapsto\operatorname{Re}\bigl[\mathbf b\exp(i(\mathbf k\cdot\mathbf x-\omega t))\bigr]$$ on $\mathbb R^3$, componentwise. Complex notation is an encoding of real fields and of real linear equations; the complex object is not itself a physical field, and real parts, imaginary parts and complex conjugation are explicit operations.
current_object.strategy: State the encoding convention and its regularity: the defining maps are smooth in $(\mathbf x,t)$ because the complex exponential is entire and $(\mathbf x,t)\mapsto\mathbf k\cdot\mathbf x-\omega t$ is linear. No electromagnetic interpretation is asserted; that is a later model choice.

current_object.title: The electric and magnetic fields as fixed-time spatial vector fields
current_object.statement: Let the laboratory region $U\cong I\times\Omega$, its spatial Euclidean structure and its units be those of [[def-em-lab-geometry]] and [[def-em-si-conventions]], and let $k\ge1$. An electric field of class $C^k$ on the region is a map $E:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ that is of class $C^k$ in the sense of [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]; a magnetic field of class $C^k$ is a map $B:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ of the same class. At fixed $t\in I$ the maps $E(\cdot,t),B(\cdot,t):\Omega\to\mathbb R^3$ are real spatial vector fields on the region $\Omega$, read in the $\delta$-orthonormal basis $(e_1,e_2,e_3)$ of the frame. The framework uses: $C^1$ fields in the classical Maxwell branch, $C^2$ fields where second or mixed time-space derivatives of the fields appear, and $C^\infty$ fields in the smooth existence branches; every statement carries its own regularity and no regularity beyond it is asserted. Conventions: (a) $E$ is a polar vector and $B$ an axial vector relative to the orientation of the spatial basis; the changes of inertial description adopted in [[post-sr-inertial-covariance]] are proper and orientation preserving, so orientation-reversing descriptions are not among them; (b) the fields are defined by their values on $\Omega\times I$, and no value at a point of singular source support is asserted; (c) $E$ carries V m$^{-1}$ and $B$ carries T; (d) the identification of the pair $(E,B)$ with the components of an alternating two-form, including its transformation behaviour, is made in [[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]] and is not presupposed here.

current_object.title: The ideal harmonic electric-dipole radiation model
current_object.reference: scaffold-added necessary model definition for the dipole scattering and Thomson items (see research/physics-em-sr-40-2026-10-08-batch-40.notes.md)
current_object.statement: Let $\omega>0$, $k:=\omega/c$ with $c$ the vacuum speed of [[def-em-si-conventions]], $\mu_0>0$ the vacuum permeability of [[def-em-si-conventions]], and $p_0\in\mathbb C^3$ (the complex dipole-moment amplitude, in $\mathrm C\,\mathrm m$). Define, on the punctured space $\mathbb R^3\setminus\{0\}$ and all times $t\in\mathbb R$, $$E_{\rm d}(x,t):=\operatorname{Re}\Bigl(-\frac{\mu_0\omega^2}{4\pi r}\,n\times(n\times p_0)\,e^{i(kr-\omega t)}\Bigr),\qquad B_{\rm d}(x,t):=\frac1c\,n\times E_{\rm d}(x,t),$$ where $r:=|x|$ and $n:=x/r$ ([[def-euclidean-inner-product]], [[def-cross-product-in-r3]]), with the real part and complex exponential of [[def-complex-conjugate-real-imaginary-part-and-modulus]] and [[def-complex-exponential]] and the real-field encoding of [[def-em-complex-plane-wave]]. Call $(E_{\rm d},B_{\rm d})$ the **ideal harmonic electric-dipole radiation model of frequency $\omega$ and amplitude $p_0$**, and call $S_{\rm d}:=E_{\rm d}\times B_{\rm d}/\mu_0$ its model flux ([[def-em-vacuum-energy-flux]]); the model fields are read as an electric and a magnetic field of [[def-em-fields]]. [Adopted status] This is an explicitly adopted ideal radiation-law model, fixed by the following declarations: (i) it is the leading transverse far-zone field of [[pthm-em-dipole-radiation]](c) evaluated at the harmonic transverse moment $V(u)=\operatorname{Re}(-\omega^2p_0e^{-i\omega u})$, i.e. at $p''$ for the waveform $p(u)=\operatorname{Re}(p_0e^{-i\omega u})$; (ii) the model contains no independent magnetic-dipole or higher-multipole radiation, no near-zone or static field and no other radiating component; (iii) it is not asserted to solve the vacuum Maxwell equations at finite $r$, to be the field of any actual source, to satisfy any boundary condition or to have finite total energy on $\mathbb R^3\setminus\{0\}$; (iv) for compact smooth conserved sources the difference from the actual retarded fields is controlled only by the explicit absolute bounds of [[pthm-em-dipole-radiation]]. No measured, empirical or material-response content is adopted: $p_0$ is prescribed model data, not a derived polarizability.

current_object.title: Laboratory geometry: a restricted inertial chart, its spatial slices and fixed-time fields
current_object.statement:
Let $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ be an oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski space ([[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]]), let $(o;e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ be an inertial frame with inertial chart $x:A\to\mathbb R^4$ ([[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]]), let $c>0$ be the framework's conversion constant, and let $\delta$ be the Euclidean spatial form of that frame on $n^\perp$, $n:=e_0$, with norm $|\cdot|$ and positive spatial orientation ([[def-spatial-euclidean-structure-of-an-inertial-frame]]). Fix a nonempty open interval $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ ([[def-interval]]) and a nonempty open set $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^3$, and put

$$U:=\{p\in A:\ \text{there are }t\in I,\ y\in\Omega\text{ with }x^0(p)=ct,\ (x^1,x^2,x^3)(p)=y\}.$$

Then: (a) [Chart restriction] $x(U)=\{(ct,y):t\in I,\ y\in\Omega\}$ and $\Phi:U\to I\times\Omega$, $\Phi(p):=(x^0(p)/c,(x^1,x^2,x^3)(p))$, is a bijection, because the inertial chart $x:A\to\mathbb R^4$ is a bijection and $c>0$; its components are the laboratory time coordinate $t(p):=x^0(p)/c$ and the laboratory position $r(p):=(x^1(p),x^2(p),x^3(p))$. (b) [Slices and spatial structure] For each $t\in I$ the slice $U_t:=\{p\in U:t(p)=t\}$ is carried bijectively onto $\Omega$ by $r$; the constant vector $n=e_0$ is future unit timelike, and $(e_1,e_2,e_3)$ is the $\delta$-orthonormal positively oriented basis of $n^\perp$ in which the coordinates of $r$ are expressed. (c) [Laboratory fields] A laboratory field of rank $m$ is a map $F:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R^m$; it is identified with the map $U\to\mathbb R^m$, $p\mapsto F(r(p),t(p))$, and with the family $(F(\cdot,t))_{t\in I}$ of maps $\Omega\to\mathbb R^m$, its values at fixed time. Such a field is of class $C^k$ when the map $(y,t)\mapsto F(y,t)$ is $C^k$ in the sense of [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]; then $\partial_{y_i}F$ (at fixed $t$) and $\partial_tF$ (at fixed $y$) are the partial derivatives of [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]]. No regularity of a field is asserted beyond the class stated for it. (d) [Conventions] The product decomposition is a coordinate identification inside the single inertial frame $(o;e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$; it is not a Galilean transformation, it does not compare two inertial frames, and it does not assert absolute simultaneity. The objects $I,\Omega,t,r,\delta$ and the identification $\mathbb R^3\cong n^\perp$ belong to the named frame; changes of inertial description are the proper orthochronous maps adopted in [[post-sr-inertial-covariance]]. The frame is an origin together with an ordered basis; it is not a congruence of observers, and no moving observer field is defined here.
current_object.strategy: A construction definition with elementary verifications. The inertial chart $x$ of [[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]] is a bijection, so its restriction to the set of events whose chart coordinates lie in $cI\times\Omega$ has image $cI\times\Omega$; composing with the bijection $cI\times\Omega\to I\times\Omega$, $(ct,y)\mapsto(t,y)$ (bijective because $c>0$) gives the bijection $\Phi$. Each slice $U_t$ is $\Phi^{-1}(\{t\}\times\Omega)$, on which $r$ restricts to a bijection onto $\Omega$. The claims about $n$, $(e_1,e_2,e_3)$, $\delta$ and the orientation are exactly the content of [[def-spatial-euclidean-structure-of-an-inertial-frame]]; the $C^k$ notion is that of [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]] and the two kinds of partial derivative are those of [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]] applied to the product coordinates. Clause (d) records conventions only: the frame dependence of $r,\delta$ and slices is stated rather than hidden, and no Galilean or observer-congruence claim is made. Nothing here uses a theorem of the framework, and the laboratory region may be a proper subset of $A$; no global chart of $A$ other than the given inertial chart is asserted.

Fix a nonempty open interval $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ ([[def-interval]]) and a nonempty open set $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^3$, and put

$$U:=\{p\in A:\ \text{there are }t\in I,\ y\in\Omega\text{ with }x^0(p)=ct,\ (x^1,x^2,x^3)(p)=y\}.$$

Then: (a) [Chart restriction] $x(U)=\{(ct,y):t\in I,\ y\in\Omega\}$ and $\Phi:U\to I\times\Omega$, $\Phi(p):=(x^0(p)/c,(x^1,x^2,x^3)(p))$, is a bijection, because the inertial chart $x:A\to\mathbb R^4$ is a bijection and $c>0$; its components are the laboratory time coordinate $t(p):=x^0(p)/c$ and the laboratory position $r(p):=(x^1(p),x^2(p),x^3(p))$. (b) [Slices and spatial structure] For each $t\in I$ the slice $U_t:=\{p\in U:t(p)=t\}$ is carried bijectively onto $\Omega$ by $r$; the constant vector $n=e_0$ is future unit timelike, and $(e_1,e_2,e_3)$ is the $\delta$-orthonormal positively oriented basis of $n^\perp$ in which the coordinates of $r$ are expressed. (c) [Laboratory fields] A laboratory field of rank $m$ is a map $F:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R^m$; it is identified with the map $U\to\mathbb R^m$, $p\mapsto F(r(p),t(p))$, and with the family $(F(\cdot,t))_{t\in I}$ of maps $\Omega\to\mathbb R^m$, its values at fixed time. Such a field is of class $C^k$ when the map $(y,t)\mapsto F(y,t)$ is $C^k$ in the sense of [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]; then $\partial_{y_i}F$ (at fixed $t$) and $\partial_tF$ (at fixed $y$) are the partial derivatives of [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]]. No regularity of a field is asserted beyond the class stated for it. (d) [Conventions] The product decomposition is a coordinate identification inside the single inertial frame $(o;e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$; it is not a Galilean transformation, it does not compare two inertial frames, and it does not assert absolute simultaneity. The objects $I,\Omega,t,r,\delta$ and the identification $\mathbb R^3\cong n^\perp$ belong to the named frame; changes of inertial description are the proper orthochronous maps adopted in [[post-sr-inertial-covariance]]. The frame is an origin together with an ordered basis; it is not a congruence of observers, and no moving observer field is defined here.
used_after_object.strategy: A construction definition with elementary verifications. The inertial chart $x$ of [[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]] is a bijection, so its restriction to the set of events whose chart coordinates lie in $cI\times\Omega$ has image $cI\times\Omega$; composing with the bijection $cI\times\Omega\to I\times\Omega$, $(ct,y)\mapsto(t,y)$ (bijective because $c>0$) gives the bijection $\Phi$. Each slice $U_t$ is $\Phi^{-1}(\{t\}\times\Omega)$, on which $r$ restricts to a bijection onto $\Omega$. The claims about $n$, $(e_1,e_2,e_3)$, $\delta$ and the orientation are exactly the content of [[def-spatial-euclidean-structure-of-an-inertial-frame]]; the $C^k$ notion is that of [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]] and the two kinds of partial derivative are those of [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]] applied to the product coordinates. current_object.title: Real plane-wave fields encoded by complex amplitudes
current_object.statement: Fix a wavevector $k\in\mathbb R^3\setminus\{0\}$ and a positive angular frequency $\omega>0$ ($k$ carries $\mathrm m^{-1}$ and $\omega$ the unit $\mathrm s^{-1}$ in the SI conventions of [[def-em-si-conventions]]), and fix complex amplitudes $e,b\in\mathbb C^3$, where $e$ carries the unit $\mathrm V\,\mathrm m^{-1}$ and $b$ the unit T of the electric and magnetic fields of [[def-em-fields]]. Let $k\cdot x$ denote the Euclidean inner product of [[def-euclidean-inner-product]], and let $\exp$ and $\operatorname{Re}$ be those of the encoding definition [[def-em-complex-plane-wave]], whose convention that physical fields are the real parts of complex expressions is used throughout. Define, for each $t\in\mathbb R$, maps $E(\cdot,t),B(\cdot,t):\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R^3$ by $$E(x,t):=\operatorname{Re}\bigl(e\,\exp(i(k\cdot x-\omega t))\bigr),\qquad B(x,t):=\operatorname{Re}\bigl(b\,\exp(i(k\cdot x-\omega t))\bigr),$$ componentwise, and put $|k|:=\sqrt{\langle k,k\rangle}$, $\hat k:=k/|k|$ and $T:=2\pi/\omega$. Terminology: $k$ is the **wavevector**, $\hat k$ the **propagation direction**, $|k|$ the **wavenumber**, $\omega$ the **angular frequency**, $T$ the **period**, $e,b$ the **complex amplitudes**, and $\theta(x,t):=k\cdot x-\omega t$ the **phase**. Then: (a) [Objects, domain and regularity] Both maps are of class $C^\infty$ on $\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R$ in the sense of [[def-em-complex-plane-wave]]; on the whole-space laboratory region $\Omega=\mathbb R^3$, $I=\mathbb R$ of [[def-em-lab-geometry]] they are an electric and a magnetic field of [[def-em-fields]] of every finite class $C^k$, $k\ge1$, read in the frame basis $(e_1,e_2,e_3)$. (b) [Phase and periodicity] At fixed $x$ the map $t\mapsto\theta(x,t)$ is affine with derivative $-\omega<0$, so the phase decreases in time (the $e^{-i\omega t}$ convention); $E$ and $B$ depend on $(x,t)$ only through $\theta$ and are $T$-periodic in $t$. (c) [Zero and nonzero waves] $(E,B)$ is the identically zero pair on $\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R$ if and only if $e=b=0$; call the wave **nonzero** otherwise. The electric field alone determines $e$ and the magnetic field alone determines $b$, because $\operatorname{Re}(w\,e^{i\theta})=0$ for all real $\theta$ forces $w=0$ (evaluate at $\theta=0$ and at $\theta=\pi/2$). (d) [Status] This item fixes objects, conventions and terminology only. It asserts no field equation, no dispersion relation, no transversality, no energy claim and no polarisation classification; those are the content of [[pthm-em-plane-wave-maxwell]] and [[def-em-polarization-definition]]. The units and the propagation constant $c$ are those of [[def-em-si-conventions]], and no empirical realisation or measurement is claimed.

current_object.title: Framework-local SI units, the vacuum constants and the exact/measured status of their values
current_object.statement: Adopt the SI system of units for this framework, with the following quantity table and conventions; every symbol is a quantity of this framework and the laboratory structure is that of [[def-em-lab-geometry]]. (a) [Coordinates and constants] $x^0=ct$ and each spatial coordinate $x^i$ carries the metre (m); the time coordinate $t$ carries the second (s); the conversion constant $c>0$ carries m s$^{-1}$ and has the exact SI defining value $c=299\,792\,458\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$; the elementary charge $e$ has the exact SI defining value $e=1.602\,176\,634\times10^{-19}\ \mathrm{C}$, and this item does not assert that physical charge is quantised; the magnetic constant $\mu_0>0$ carries N A$^{-2}$ and is measured, so no exact numerical value of $\mu_0$ is asserted (the pre-2019 SI fixed the historical nominal $\mu_{0,\mathrm{nom}}:=4\pi\times10^{-7}\ \mathrm{H\,m^{-1}}=4\pi\times10^{-7}\ \mathrm{N\,A^{-2}}$ exactly; since the revised SI took effect on 20 May 2019, $\mu_0$ is experimentally determined. The SI brochure quotes the nominal $\mu_{0,\mathrm{nom}}$ as the estimate at the 2019 adoption with relative standard uncertainty $2.3\times10^{-10}$; this is historical estimate/uncertainty context, not an exact equality for the actual $\mu_0$ or a current measured value); the electric constant is defined within the framework by $\varepsilon_0:=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$ in F m$^{-1}$, consistent with the exact SI relation $\varepsilon_0\mu_0=1/c^2$, so that $c^2\varepsilon_0\mu_0=1$ and $\varepsilon_0$ inherits the relative standard uncertainty of $\mu_0$. (b) [Electromagnetic quantities] Charge $q$ carries the coulomb (C); the charge density $\rho$ of [[def-em-sources]] carries C m$^{-3}$ and the current density $J$ carries A m$^{-2}$, so that the four-current components $(c\rho,J)$ carry A m$^{-2}$; the electric field $E$ carries V m$^{-1}$; the magnetic field $B$ carries the tesla (T), where $1\ \mathrm{T}=1\ \mathrm{N\,A^{-1}\,m^{-1}}$; the scalar potential $\varphi$ carries V and the vector potential $A$ carries T m, so that the four-potential components $(\varphi/c,A)$ carry T m; the components of the electromagnetic two-form of [[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]] carry T; a force carries the newton (N), $1\ \mathrm{N}=1\ \mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-2}}$. (c) [Mechanical quantities] A rest mass parameter $m$ carries the kilogram (kg) and a four-momentum $P=mU$ carries kg m s$^{-1}$ ([[post-sr-massive-particle-dynamics]]); field energy density carries J m$^{-3}$, energy flux W m$^{-2}$, so that $1\ \mathrm{W}=1\ \mathrm{J\,s^{-1}}=1\ \mathrm{V\,A}$. (d) [Bookkeeping only] The unit of a quantity records the adopted system of units; it does not show that a quantity is primitive in this or any other framework, it contains no measurement, and it does not identify a quantity with a similarly named quantity of another framework. The exact defining values of $c$ and $e$ fix numerical conventions of the SI, they do not by themselves identify $c$ with the vacuum propagation constant of ideal light, which is the physical adoption of [[post-em-minkowski-physical-model]].
current_object.strategy: A convention definition: it fixes the coordinate normalisation $x^0=ct$, the unit of each quantity used in this framework, the exact SI defining values of $c$ and $e$ and the measured status of $\mu_0$. The exact values $c=299\,792\,458$ m/s and $e=1.602\,176\,634\times10^{-19}$ C, and the statements that the new definition of the ampere fixes $e$ rather than $\mu_0$, that $\mu_0$ must now be determined experimentally, and that $\varepsilon_0\mu_0=1/c^2$ remains exact, are taken from the SI brochure's defining-constants table and its ampere section. The framework's definition of $\varepsilon_0$ by $(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$ is a definition consistent with that exact relation; the uncertainty carried by $\varepsilon_0$ is recorded rather than hidden. The dimensional checks of the framework's equations and couplings are developed on the companion examples page of this pair. No exact or current measured numerical value of $\mu_0$ is asserted and no experiment is claimed. The historical nominal and adoption uncertainty are explicitly source context, not a substitution for the current experimentally determined constant.

current_object.statement:
Let the laboratory region and its chart be those of [[def-em-lab-geometry]], with the units of [[def-em-si-conventions]]. current_object.title: Vacuum electromagnetic energy density and energy flux (the Poynting vector)
current_object.statement:
Let $U\cong I\times\Omega$, its spatial Euclidean structure, its frame basis $(e_1,e_2,e_3)$ and its SI conventions be those of [[def-em-lab-geometry]] and [[def-em-si-conventions]], and let $E,B:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ be an electric and a magnetic field of [[def-em-fields]] of class $C^k$ with $k\ge1$. Define the **electromagnetic energy density** $u$ and the **energy flux density** (Poynting vector) $S$ by
$$u(x,t):=\frac{\varepsilon_0\lvert E(x,t)\rvert^2}{2}+\frac{\lvert B(x,t)\rvert^2}{2\mu_0},\qquad S(x,t):=\frac{1}{\mu_0}\,E(x,t)\times B(x,t),$$
where $\lvert E\rvert^2=\langle E,E\rangle$ uses the Euclidean inner product of [[def-euclidean-inner-product]], $\times$ is the cross product of [[def-cross-product-in-r3]] in the frame basis, and $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$ is the constant of [[def-em-si-conventions]]. Then $u:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R$ and $S:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ are of class $C^k$ in the sense of [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]] (they are polynomials in the components of $E,B$), with $u$ in $\mathrm J\,\mathrm m^{-3}=\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm m^{-1}\mathrm s^{-2}$ and $S$ in $\mathrm W\,\mathrm m^{-2}=\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm s^{-3}$; at fixed $t\in I$, $u(\cdot,t):\Omega\to\mathbb R$ is a real-valued function and $S(\cdot,t):\Omega\to\mathbb R^3$ a spatial vector field on $\Omega$, read in $(e_1,e_2,e_3)$.
(a) [Pointwise definition] The definitions use only the values of $E,B$ at the same point $(x,t)$; no derivative of the fields and no convention beyond the fixed laboratory frame is used. (b) [Products and singular support] If $E,B$ are only locally integrable (the weak branch of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]]), the products $E_iE_j$, $B_iB_j$ and the components of $E\times B$ need not be locally integrable and no product of distributions is defined: the displayed formulas then define $u$ and $S$ pointwise almost everywhere, and the framework uses them only where the local integrability of the products, respectively of the component being integrated, is separately established. No value of $u$ or $S$ is assigned at a point of singular source support. (c) [Quadratic character] $u$ and $S$ are quadratic in the fields, so decompositions of the fields do not make $u$ or $S$ additive; cross terms generally contribute. (d) [Status] This item defines quantities only; the interpretation of $u$ and $S$ as an energy density and an energy flux is the content of [[pthm-em-poynting-balance]], and no identification of $(u,S)$ with components of a covariant tensor is made here.

The claim that $u$ and $S$ are again of class $C^k$ is the sum/product/composition calculus of [[thm-chain-sum-product-and-composition-rules-for-banach-derivatives]] read componentwise. current_object.statement: Let $\omega>0$, $T:=2\pi/\omega$, $n\ge1$ and $w\in\mathbb C^n$; use the real part and complex exponential of [[def-complex-conjugate-real-imaginary-part-and-modulus]] and [[def-complex-exponential]]. Define $z_p:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R^n$ by $z_p(t):=\operatorname{Re}(-w\omega^{-2}e^{-i\omega t})$ componentwise ([[def-derivative]] for the derivative below). Then: (a) $z_p$ is $C^\infty$ ([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]) and satisfies $z_p''(t)=\operatorname{Re}(we^{-i\omega t})$ for every $t\in\mathbb R$; it is $T$-periodic. (b) every $C^2$ solution $z:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R^n$ of $z''(t)=\operatorname{Re}(we^{-i\omega t})$ on $\mathbb R$ has the form $z(t)=z_p(t)+a+bt$ with unique $a,b\in\mathbb R^n$. (c) such a solution is $T$-periodic if and only if $b=0$; the $T$-periodic solutions are exactly $z_p(t)+a$, $a\in\mathbb R^n$, and their oscillating part has complex amplitude $-w/\omega^2$.
current_object.strategy: (a) By the Cartesian form and Euler identity of [[cor-complex-exponential-cartesian-form-modulus-and-eulers-identity]], $z_p(t)=-\omega^{-2}[(\operatorname{Re}w)\cos(\omega t)+(\operatorname{Im}w)\sin(\omega t)]$ componentwise. Differentiating twice with the sum, scalar-multiple and product rules of [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]] and the derivatives of [[thm-sine-and-cosine-derivatives]] gives $z_p''=\operatorname{Re}w\cos(\omega t)+\operatorname{Im}w\sin(\omega t)=\operatorname{Re}(we^{-i\omega t})$. Periodicity of $z_p$ follows from $e^{-i\omega(t+T)}=e^{-i\omega t}e^{-i\omega T}=e^{-i\omega t}$ by the addition law of [[thm-complex-exponential-addition-and-real-extension]] and $e^{-2\pi i}=1$, the latter from the Cartesian form and the values $\cos2\pi=1$, $\sin2\pi=0$ of [[thm-sine-cosine-zero-sets-and-fundamental-period]]. (b) If $z$ is any $C^2$ solution, then $h:=z-z_p$ satisfies $h''=0$ on $\mathbb R$. Apply [[cor-zero-derivative-implies-constant]] on the interval $\mathbb R$ ([[def-interval]]) to each component of $h'$: $h'=b$ is constant. current_object.reference: scaffold-added necessary mathematical prerequisite for the dipole and emitted-power items (see research/physics-em-sr-40-2026-10-08-batch-36.notes.md)
current_object.statement: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$), as carried by the surface-measure interface below ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $\sigma$ be the polar surface measure on the unit sphere $S^2\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ ([[def-polar-surface-measure-on-the-unit-sphere]]), let $e_3:=(0,0,1)$ be the third coordinate unit vector and write $n_3=n\cdot e_3$ for $n\in S^2$. Then: (a) [Zonal identity] for every continuous $f:[-1,1]\to\mathbb R$, $$\int_{S^2}f(n_3)\,d\sigma(n)=2\pi\int_{-1}^{1}f(u)\,du.$$ (b) [Linear weighted moment] for every continuous $f$ and every $a\in\mathbb R^3$, $$\int_{S^2}(n\cdot a)\,f(n_3)\,d\sigma(n)=2\pi\,a_3\int_{-1}^{1}u\,f(u)\,du.$$ (c) [Quadratic weighted moment] for every continuous $f$ and every $a\in\mathbb R^3$, $$\int_{S^2}(n\cdot a)^2f(n_3)\,d\sigma(n)=2\pi\,a_3^{2}\int_{-1}^{1}u^{2}f(u)\,du+\pi\,(a_1^{2}+a_2^{2})\int_{-1}^{1}(1-u^{2})f(u)\,du.$$ (d) [Moments] $\sigma(S^2)=4\pi$, $\int_{S^2}n\,d\sigma=0$, $\int_{S^2}n_in_j\,d\sigma=(4\pi/3)\delta_{ij}$, and for every $a\in\mathbb R^3$ $\int_{S^2}(n\cdot a)^2d\sigma=(4\pi/3)|a|^2$ and $\int_{S^2}|n\times a|^2d\sigma=(8\pi/3)|a|^2$, where $\delta_{ij}$ is the Kronecker symbol and $\times$ the cross product of [[def-cross-product-in-r3]]. (e) [Scope] (a)-(d) are identities for the polar surface measure of the unit sphere with only the stated continuity of $f$; they assert no physical field, flux or radiation statement. The measure is finite, so all displayed integrals are absolutely convergent; $f$ need not be nonnegative. For the uses on this page $f$ is a rational function with denominator bounded below by $1-b>0$, hence continuous on $[-1,1]$.
current_object.strategy: Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. (a) Parametrize $S^2$ by $X(\theta,\varphi):=(\sin\theta\cos\varphi,\ \sin\theta\sin\varphi,\ \cos\theta)$ on $[0,\pi]\times[0,2\pi]$. Computing the coordinate cross product with the sin/cos derivatives and the Pythagorean identity ([[thm-sine-and-cosine-derivatives]], [[cor-trigonometric-parity-and-pythagorean-identity]], [[def-cross-product-in-r3]]) gives $X_\theta\times X_\varphi=\sin\theta\,X(\theta,\varphi)$, whose norm is $\sin\theta\ge0$; by [[thm-surface-area-density-is-cross-product-norm]] and [[def-surface-area-and-scalar-surface-integral-of-a-patch]] the chart surface integral of $F(n)=f(n_3)$ is $\int_0^{2\pi}\int_0^{\pi}f(\cos\theta)\sin\theta\,d\theta\,d\varphi$, with the seam and the poles lying on the parameter boundary exactly as in the sphere-area computation, so this is the integral over $S^2$ ([[def-surface-integral-on-a-compact-c-one-hypersurface]], [[lem-parameter-boundary-exceptions-do-not-affect-surface-integrals|the boundary-exception convention]]). The chart measure equals the polar measure $\sigma$ ([[lem-euclidean-chart-measure-agrees-with-polar-surface-measure]]). By [[thm-jordan-fubini-by-sections]] the $\varphi$-integral is the constant $2\pi$, and with $P(u):=\int_0^u f$ ([[thm-ftc-first-part]]) the chain rule and [[thm-ftc-second-part]] give $\int_0^{\pi}f(\cos\theta)\sin\theta\,d\theta=[-P(\cos\theta)]_0^{\pi}=P(1)-P(-1)=\int_{-1}^{1}f(u)\,du$, using $\cos0=1$, $\cos\pi=-1$ and the derivative $\cos'=-\sin$ ([[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]], [[thm-sine-and-cosine-derivatives]]). The maps $\eta_1(n_1,n_2,n_3):=(-n_1,n_2,n_3)$ and $\eta_2(n_1,n_2,n_3):=(n_1,-n_2,n_3)$ are orthogonal and preserve $\sigma$ ([[lem-euclidean-chart-measure-agrees-with-polar-surface-measure]]); since $n_1f(n_3)$ and $n_2f(n_3)$ change sign under $\eta_1$ and $\eta_2$ respectively, the substitution formula for the measure-preserving involution $\eta_i$ (indicators by definition, simple functions by linearity, bounded Borel functions by the usual approximation, exactly as in the vanishing-first-moment computation of [[lem-first-moment-of-the-unit-sphere-vanishes]]) gives $\int n_if(n_3)d\sigma=-\int n_if(n_3)d\sigma=0$ for $i=1,2$; the remaining term is $a_3\int n_3f(n_3)d\sigma=2\pi a_3\int_{-1}^1uf(u)du$ by (a) applied to $F(u)=uf(u)$. (c) Expanding the square, the mixed terms $n_in_jf(n_3)$ with $i\ne j$ vanish by the same reflection argument; the terms $n_1^2$ and $n_2^2$ are equal by the swap $(n_1,n_2,n_3)\mapsto(n_2,n_1,n_3)$, which is orthogonal and preserves $\sigma$. Hence $\int n_1^2f(n_3)d\sigma=\int n_2^2f(n_3)d\sigma=\tfrac12\int(1-n_3^2)f(n_3)d\sigma=\pi\int_{-1}^1(1-u^2)f(u)du$ by (a) applied to $F(u)=(1-u^2)f(u)$, while $\int n_3^2f(n_3)d\sigma=2\pi\int_{-1}^1u^2f(u)du$ by (a) applied to $F(u)=u^2f(u)$; linearity of the $\sigma$-integral on the (finite-measure) integrable functions is [[thm-linearity-of-the-lebesgue-integral-on-l-one]]. This proves (c). (d) Taking $f=1$ in (a) gives $\sigma(S^2)=2\pi\cdot2=4\pi$, which also evaluates the closed form of [[cor-volume-of-the-unit-n-ball]] at $n=3$ together with the Gamma values $\Gamma(5/2)=(3/2)(1/2)\Gamma(1/2)=3\sqrt\pi/4$ ([[thm-real-gamma-functional-equation]], [[cor-real-gamma-one-half-is-root-pi]]), so the two routes agree. Taking $f=1$ in (b),(c) gives $\int n_if(n_3)=0$ for $i=1,2$ and the matrix identity $\int n_in_jd\sigma=(4\pi/3)\delta_{ij}$ (equivalently $\int(n\cdot a)^2d\sigma=(4\pi/3)|a|^2$); the first moment statement is the three-dimensional case of [[lem-first-moment-of-the-unit-sphere-vanishes]]. Finally $|n\times a|^2=|a|^2-(n\cdot a)^2$ by the cross-product norm identity ([[def-cross-product-in-r3]], [[def-euclidean-inner-product]]), so $\int|n\times a|^2d\sigma=4\pi|a|^2-(4\pi/3)|a|^2=(8\pi/3)|a|^2$. current_object.title: Controlled electric-dipole far field and retarded-time radiated power of a compact smooth source
current_object.statement: Assume the setting and hypotheses of [[thm-em-radiation-asymptotic-flux]] and $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ as carried by its suppliers: $c>0$, $\mu_0>0$, $a>0$, $t_0<T$, jointly $C^\infty$ fields $\rho,J$ vanishing outside $\overline B_a(0)\times[t_0,T]$ and satisfying $\partial_t\rho+\operatorname{div}J=0$; let $\varphi,A$ be the retarded potentials and $E:=-\nabla\varphi-\partial_tA$, $B:=\nabla\times A$ the fields, with $S:=E\times B/\mu_0$ ([[def-em-vacuum-energy-flux]], [[pthm-em-poynting-balance]]). Adopt the causal selection [[post-em-radiation-selection]]: these retarded fields are the fields of the source model (the compact smooth instance established by [[pthm-em-retarded-potentials]]). Define the **time-dependent electric dipole moment** $$p(u):=\int_{B_a}y\,\rho(y,u)\,dy\in\mathbb R^3$$ (componentwise, about the fixed chart origin of [[def-em-lab-geometry]]; it is the fixed-time analogue of the static source moment of [[def-em-electric-moments]]), and, as in the asymptotic theorem, $I(n,u):=\int_{B_a}J(y,u+n\cdot y/c)\,dy$, $V(n,u):=\partial_uI(n,u)=\int_{B_a}J_t(y,u+n\cdot y/c)\,dy$ and $$D(u):=\frac{a}{c}\int_{B_a}\sup_{|v-u|\le a/c}|J_{tt}(y,v)|\,dy.$$ Then: (a) [Moment identities] $p\in C^\infty(\mathbb R;\mathbb R^3)$, $p'(u)=\int_{B_a}J(y,u)\,dy$, $p''(u)=\int_{B_a}J_t(y,u)\,dy$, $\int_{B_a}\rho_t(y,u)\,dy=0$ and the total charge $\int_{B_a}\rho(y,u)\,dy$ vanishes for every $u$. (b) [Dipole replacement error] $|V(n,u)-p''(u)|\le D(u)$ for every $n\in S^2$ and every $u\in[t_0,T]$: the explicit absolute error of the dipole approximation to the source's transverse current moment. (c) [Leading fields] With $\Gamma_E$, $\Gamma_B$ the constants of [[thm-em-radiation-asymptotic-flux]](b) (depending only on $a,c,\mu_0$ and the listed source suprema), for every $n\in S^2$, $u\in[t_0,T]$, $r\ge2a$: $$\Bigl|E\bigl(rn,u+\tfrac rc\bigr)-\frac{\mu_0}{4\pi r}n\times(n\times p''(u))\Bigr|\le\frac{\Gamma_E}{r^2}+\frac{\mu_0D(u)}{4\pi r},\qquad \Bigl|B\bigl(rn,u+\tfrac rc\bigr)-\frac{n\times E(rn,u+\tfrac rc)}{c}\Bigr|\le\frac{\Gamma_B+\Gamma_E/c}{r^2}.$$ The leading far field is the electric-dipole field, with amplitude proportional to $p''(u)$; all errors are uniform in the direction $n$ at fixed $u$. (d) [Retarded-time radiated power] The limit of [[thm-em-radiation-asymptotic-flux]](c) equals $\mu_0|p''(u)|^2/(6\pi c)+R(u)$ with the explicit absolute error $$|R(u)|\le\frac{\mu_0\bigl(2|p''(u)|D(u)+D(u)^2\bigr)}{4\pi c},\qquad\text{so}\qquad \lim_{r\to\infty}\int_{S^2}r^2n\cdot S\bigl(rn,u+\tfrac rc\bigr)d\sigma=\frac{\mu_0}{6\pi c}|p''(u)|^2\ \text{ whenever } D(u)=0.$$ The evaluation uses the sphere moment $\int_{S^2}|n\times p''|^2d\sigma=(8\pi/3)|p''|^2$ of [[lem-em-sphere-zonal-moments]](d). The limit is at fixed retarded time $u$, not at fixed observation time. (e) [Scope] The compact smooth source branch only; the dipole error is absolute and explicitly controlled by $D(u)$, and no assertion is made that slow or 'nonrelativistic' source motion alone makes $D(u)$ small -- that is a hypothesis on the source's time variation. No point charge, no moving point source, no radiation reaction, no self-force and no empirical or measurement content; the failure of the correspondence with an oscillator for rapidly varying sources is retained through $D(u)$. Separately retain the sharper actual source estimate $|B(rn,u+r/c)-n\times E_{\rm lead}(n,u,r)/c|\le\Gamma_B/r^2$, with $E_{\rm lead}=\mu_0n\times(n\times V)/(4\pi r)$; the bound against the actual E uses the combined constant displayed in(c).
current_object.strategy: Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ as carried by [[thm-em-radiation-asymptotic-flux]]. (a) $\rho$ is $C^\infty$ with compact support, so $u\mapsto p(u)$ is $C^\infty$ by differentiation under the integral sign ([[lem-em-parameter-integrals]]) and $p'(u)=\int y\,\rho_t(y,u)dy$; integrating by parts componentwise over a ball containing the support via the divergence theorem ([[thm-divergence-theorem-for-bounded-c-one-euclidean-domains]], boundary term zero by compact support) gives $\int y_i\partial_t\rho\,dy=-\int y_i\operatorname{div}J\,dy=\int J_i\,dy$, since $\partial_i(y_iJ_k)$ contributes $J_i$ and the remaining divergence term integrates to zero. Replacing $J$ by $J_t$ (equivalently differentiating in $u$ under the integral sign) gives $p''=\int J_t$. The vanishing $\int\rho_t=0$ is the same divergence theorem with weight $1$ (equivalently clause (f) of [[pthm-em-retarded-potentials]]), and the total charge vanishes because $\rho$ is supported in $t\in[t_0,T]$. (b) For fixed $y\in B_a$ the one-variable function $v\mapsto J_t(y,v)$ is $C^1$ on the interval between $u$ and $u+n\cdot y/c$, whose length is at most $a/c$; for nonzero vector difference w choose its fixed unit direction e=w/|w| and apply the scalar mean value theorem ([[cor-mean-value-theorem]]) to e dot J_t; finite Euclidean Cauchy-Schwarz bounds |e dot J_tt| by |J_tt| (the zero difference is immediate), giving $|J_t(y,u+n\cdot y/c)-J_t(y,u)|\le(a/c)\sup_{|v-u|\le a/c}|J_{tt}(y,v)|$ componentwise, and integrating over $B_a$ with the integral triangle inequality and monotonicity ([[thm-integral-triangle-inequality]], [[prop-order-and-scalar-rules-for-the-nonnegative-integral]]) gives (b). (e) records that the error coefficient $D(u)$ constrains the source's own time variation and that the limit is a fixed-retarded-time limit, as in the supplier; no self-force, point-source, decay or empirical claim is added.

current_object.title: Differential and total cross sections of the ideal harmonic dipole in a plane-wave field
current_object.statement: Assume Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$) as carried by [[pthm-em-dipole-radiation]] and [[lem-em-sphere-zonal-moments]] ([[def-countable-choice]]); the period-average and cross-section algebra itself uses no choice. Adopt the ideal harmonic electric-dipole radiation model of [[def-em-ideal-harmonic-dipole-model]] with frequency $\omega>0$, wavenumber $k=\omega/c$ and amplitude $p_0\in\mathbb C^3$; let $E_{\rm d},B_{\rm d},S_{\rm d}$ be its fields and model flux. current_object.title: The four-force equation reproduces the coordinate Lorentz force and power
current_object.statement: Assume the framework's spacetime, field and worldline objects of [[post-em-minkowski-physical-model]], [[def-em-lab-geometry]], [[def-em-fields]] and [[def-em-relativistic-worldlines-frames]], with the SI units of [[def-em-si-conventions]], and clause (i) of the adopted Lorentz coupling [[post-em-lorentz-coupling]]: a constant charge parameter $q\in\mathbb R$ of [[def-em-sources]] (a), an externally supplied rest mass $m>0$, a future timelike $C^2$ massive worldline $x:J\to A$ with four-velocity $U$, and a prescribed field $F$ of [[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]] that is $C^1$ on a neighbourhood of the graph of $x$ and is generated externally to the particle; the adopted equation of motion is $$m\,\frac{dU}{d\tau}=q\,\Phi(U),\qquad \eta(\Phi(u),w)=F(w,u),$$ $U$ the four-velocity of [[def-em-relativistic-worldlines-frames]] (b) with $\eta(U,U)=-c^2$. Let $t\mapsto r(t)$ be the laboratory chart reading of the worldline, $v:=r'$ its coordinate velocity and $\gamma:=(1-|v|^2/c^2)^{-1/2}$, so that $U=\gamma(c,v)$ ([[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]] (e)). Then, wherever the worldline is $C^2$: (a) [Coordinate force and power] with the coordinate three-momentum $p:=m\gamma v$ of [[pthm-sr-momentum-and-four-force]] (a), $$\frac{dp}{dt}=q\,(E+v\times B),\qquad \frac{d(\gamma mc^2)}{dt}=q\,E\cdot v,$$ the derivatives taken with respect to the chart time $t$ and $E,B$ the components of $F$ in the laboratory frame. (b) [Norm preservation] $s\mapsto\eta(U(s),U(s))$ is constant on $J$ with value $-c^2$; in particular a solution with future timelike initial data remains future timelike, and $|v(t)|<c$ wherever the reading is differentiable ([[lem-em-antisymmetric-tensor-contraction]]). (c) [Controlled low-speed expansion] for every $\delta\in(0,1)$, on any interval where $|v|/c\le\delta$, $$|\gamma-1|\le\frac{|v|^2/c^2}{2(1-\delta^2)^{3/2}},\qquad \Bigl|\gamma-1-\frac{|v|^2}{2c^2}\Bigr|\le\frac{3}{8}(1-\delta^2)^{-5/2}\Bigl(\frac{|v|^2}{c^2}\Bigr)^{2},$$ and consequently $$|p-mv|\le m|v|\,\frac{|v|^2}{2c^2(1-\delta^2)^{3/2}},\qquad \Bigl|\gamma mc^2-mc^2-\tfrac12m|v|^2\Bigr|\le\frac{3}{8}(1-\delta^2)^{-5/2}\frac{m|v|^4}{c^2};$$ the constants depend only on $\delta$, so the bounds are uniform in $|v|/c\le\delta$. These are pointwise algebraic expansions; they assert no approximation of the trajectory over a time interval, which would require a separate stability argument. (d) [Scope] The charge is constant, $m>0$ is an externally supplied parameter and $F$ is a prescribed exterior field: the particle's own field, radiation reaction and any self-force are excluded, as are magnetic monopoles and zero or variable mass; the nonrelativistic coordinate law is not adopted as exact, and (c) is a controlled kinematic expansion, not a trajectory approximation. The statement is conditional on the adopted postulates and makes no empirical claim.
current_object.strategy: **Proof technique:** contract the field with the four-velocity in the fixed component dictionary, then apply the mean value theorem to $(1-z)^{-1/2}$. (a) With $\Phi(u)^\mu=\eta^{\mu\alpha}F_{\alpha\beta}u^\beta$ ([[lem-em-antisymmetric-tensor-contraction]]) and $U=\gamma(c,v)$, $U_\nu=\gamma(-c,v)$: $q\,\Phi(U)^i=q\gamma\bigl(cF^i{}_0+F^i{}_jv^j\bigr)=q\gamma(E_i+(v\times B)_i)$ since $F^i{}_0=\eta_{00}F^{i0}=E_i/c$ and $F^i{}_j=\epsilon_{ijk}B_k$; and $q\,\Phi(U)^0=q\gamma E\cdot v/c$. Since $m\,dU^i/d\tau=q\Phi(U)^i$ and $d/dt=\gamma^{-1}d/d\tau$ ([[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]] (e)), $dp_i/dt=\gamma^{-1}\,q\gamma(E+v\times B)_i=q(E+v\times B)_i$ with $p=m\gamma v$ from [[pthm-sr-momentum-and-four-force]] (a); the temporal component gives $d(\gamma mc^2)/dt=qE\cdot v$ after multiplying by $c$. (b) $\eta(U,U)$ has derivative $2\eta(U,U')=2(q/m)\eta(U,\Phi(U))=0$ by the orthogonality clause of [[lem-em-antisymmetric-tensor-contraction]] (which needs no derivative of the field); the initial value $-c^2$ is that of the four-velocity. For the stated solution-preservation conclusion, differentiability makes $U$ continuous and the norm identity gives $(U^0)^2=c^2+|U_{\mathrm{sp}}|^2\ge c^2$. Thus $U^0$ cannot vanish; on a connected interval its sign cannot change by [[thm-intermediate-value]]. Positive initial $U^0$ therefore stays positive and the solution stays in the future timelike component. This conditional argument asserts no existence or continuation of solutions. (c) $z:=|v|^2/c^2$ and $f(z):=(1-z)^{-1/2}$; by [[thm-real-power-continuity-and-derivatives]] and [[thm-real-power-agrees-with-rational-exponent]], $f'(z)=\tfrac12(1-z)^{-3/2}$ and $f''(z)=\tfrac34(1-z)^{-5/2}$ with $a^{-r}=(a^r)^{-1}$ from [[lem-rational-power-laws]]. At $z=0$ all stated differences and bounds are zero directly; henceforth assume $0<z\le\delta^2$. The two displays for $p$ and $\gamma mc^2$ are the multiplication of these bounds by $m|v|$ and $mc^2$ ([[lem-of-abs-value]], [[def-abs-value]], [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]] for the product $p=m\gamma v$). (d) The scope clause records the postulates and exclusions; no choice principle and no empirical premise are used.

current_object.title: Period-averaged energy density, Poynting vector and momentum flux of a plane wave
current_object.statement: Let $k\in\mathbb R^3\setminus\{0\}$, $\omega>0$ with $\omega=c|k|$, let $e\in\mathbb C^3$ with $k\cdot e=0$ and $b=k\times e/\omega$, and let $(E,B)$ be the corresponding plane-wave solution of [[pthm-em-plane-wave-maxwell]] ([[def-em-plane-wave-definition]]) on $\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R$. Let $u$ and $S$ be the energy density and Poynting vector of [[def-em-vacuum-energy-flux]], and $g=S/c^2$, $\sigma$, $\Pi=-\sigma$ the momentum density, Maxwell stress and momentum flux of [[def-em-vacuum-stress-momentum]]. Write $T=2\pi/\omega$, $|e|^2=e\cdot\overline e$, $\hat k=k/|k|$, and let $\langle f\rangle:=\frac1T\int_0^Tf(x,s)\,ds$ be the period average at fixed $x$. Then, for every $x\in\mathbb R^3$: (a) [Averaged energy density] $\langle u\rangle=\frac{\varepsilon_0}{2}|e|^2$, independent of $x$ and of the starting time. (b) [Averaged Poynting vector] $\langle S\rangle=\frac{\varepsilon_0c}{2}|e|^2\hat k$; hence $\langle S\rangle=\langle u\rangle c\hat k$, and the period-averaged intensity is $I:=|\langle S\rangle|=c\langle u\rangle=\frac{\varepsilon_0c}{2}|e|^2$. (c) [Averaged momentum density, stress and momentum flux] $\langle g\rangle=\frac{\varepsilon_0}{2c}|e|^2\hat k$, and componentwise $\langle\sigma_{ij}\rangle=-\langle u\rangle\hat k_i\hat k_j$, equivalently $\langle\Pi_{ij}\rangle=\langle u\rangle\hat k_i\hat k_j$; the period-averaged momentum flux across a plane with unit normal $n$ is therefore $\langle u\rangle(\hat k\cdot n)\hat k$, a pure flux along $\hat k$ with signed coefficient $(I/c)(\hat k\cdot n)$ and magnitude $(I/c)|\hat k\cdot n|$. The tensor identity holds for every complex transverse amplitude $e$, not only for real or circular ones.
